concept.name: Exhaustion gap
concept.definition: A gap occurring near the end of an extended up or down move, typically on very high volume and a large price jump, interpreted as the final surge of euphoria or panic before the move ends. The label is only assignable with confidence in hindsight, since at the time it can be indistinguishable from a runaway gap.
concept.intuition: The last burst of FOMO buying (or panic selling) — the crowd all rushes in at once, and then there is nobody left to push further.
concept.mechanics: Identified by context: a gap late in a prolonged trend, accompanied by exceptionally high volume and often a wide open-to-close range, followed quickly by the gap being filled as price reverses. ChartSchool notes the exceptionally high volume is what separates it from a runaway gap.
concept.failure_modes: Mistaking a runaway gap for an exhaustion gap leads to premature counter-trend positioning; the two look identical at print time and are separated mainly by what volume and follow-through do next.
concept.misconceptions: That any big late-trend gap is exhaustion; trends can produce several large gaps before truly exhausting.
concept.example: After a long advance, a stock gaps up on huge volume, stalls as profit-taking dries up demand, and within days fills the gap and reverses — the exhaustion signature.

citations.source: StockCharts ChartSchool — Gaps and Gap Analysis
